data.name: Aniruddh
data.gender_notes: Aniruddh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aniruddha is a name of Lord Krishna, meaning 'Another Rudra'. Rudra is a name of Lord Shiva, meaning 'The One Who Causes Tremendous Agitation'. Aniruddha, therefore, means 'Another Shiva'. The name Aniruddh carries the meaning “Another name for Krishna” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Aniruddh usually hope their child will grow to embody another name for krishna and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aniruddh is a name of Lord Krishna, representing the power of Lord Shiva within him. It is a name of courage, victory, and loyalty.
data.etymology: Aniruddh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Another name for Krishna.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aniruddh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Buddha comes from the Sanskrit term 'Bodhi', which means 'Enlightened' or 'Awakened. It is the name of Siddhartha Gautama, who founded Buddhism.
data.spiritual_significance: Buddha's teachings of the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path offer a path to spiritual enlightenment and holds immense significance for many who seek inner peace and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Aniruddh: Unconquered, beyond the reach of maya (illusion). The supreme self, untouched by the cycle of birth and death.

historical_references.reference: Aniruddh is the name of a legendary prince in Mahabharata, the great Indian epic. He is the grandson of Krishna and the son of Prasanna, the king of Hastinapur.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian Sanskrit epic composed of over 100,000 verses in 18 books. It is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It relates the story of the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and the Kaurava princes.

historical_references.reference: Aniruddh is also mentioned in the Puranas, ancient Indian texts dealing with various aspects of Hinduism. He is considered to be an incarnation of Lord Vishnu and an avatar of Krishna.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a collection of 18 major Sanskrit texts and numerous smaller texts. They are believed to have been composed between the 4th and 8th centuries CE, although some sections may be older. They contain stories, mythology, teachings, and explanations of various aspects of Hinduism, including creation myths, genealogies of gods and heroes, descriptions of pilgrimage sites, and various cultural and philosophical teachings.
